author: macro-strategist-cyrus-daruwalla
mechanism: monthly-rebalanced NIFTY500 exposure, scalar = clip(1 - 0.5*(richness-100)/60, lo, hi), scalar known at start of month from PRIOR month-end richness (1-month lag), no transaction costs modeled.
key_finding: Full-sample, BOTH variants underperform or roughly match always-invested on Sharpe, and the leveraged (symmetric) variant makes max_drawdown WORSE (-69.4% vs -60.9%). Excluding the single 2008 GFC episode, BOTH variants modestly BEAT the benchmark (Sharpe 0.82/0.81 vs 0.79; maxDD -27.3% vs -30.0%). The entire negative full-sample verdict is driven by ONE episode: 2008-09, where richness got progressively CHEAPER as the crash continued (valuation cheapening and price still falling are NOT mutually exclusive mid-crisis), so the symmetric scalar levered UP (to 1.4x) DURING the ongoing decline before the eventual 2009 recovery, amplifying realized drawdown. The de-risk-only variant (capped at 1.0x, no leverage) avoided that specific amplification but ALSO never actually de-risked during 2008 (richness was cheap, not expensive, throughout that crash) so its maxDD matches the benchmark exactly for the full sample.
honesty_note: This is a single-episode (n=1 crisis) result driving the full-sample verdict -- classic low-n fragility, disclosed per firm protocol rather than cherry-picking the ex-2008 cut as the headline. A valuation z-score built on an EXPANDING mean/std is a slow multi-year mean-reversion signal (matches its own 5Y test having the more robust economic-logic case); applying it as a MONTHLY tactical lever mismatches horizons and can whipsaw or (in the levered variant) actively worsen drawdown during an exogenous/continuing-decline crash it was never designed to time.
verdict: NO (as a monthly leveraged scalar) / MAYBE-WEAK (as a monthly de-risk-only, no-leverage scalar -- flat-to-marginal, ex-2008 modestly positive but full-sample not clearly better than always-invested). Recommend: if used at all, apply at a LOWER rebalance frequency (quarterly/annual) as a STRATEGIC tilt, never as a levered monthly overlay, and pair with a genuinely short-horizon trigger (India VIX / breadth) for tactical de-risking rather than relying on this valuation series alone.
